_readme: Which strings in src/data may be translated. Everything else is FROZEN.
Path syntax: keys joined by '/', with '#' for an array index and '*' for any
one key. 'spells.json #/Description' means: element of the top-level array,
DEFAULT-DENY. A path not listed here fails verification if it changes. When
you believe a field should be translatable, prove it is not machine-read
(grep for the key, check src/lib) and add it here in its own commit — do not
translate first and widen the list to make the checker quiet.
'frozen_note' on each file records WHY the obvious-looking fields are not on
the list. Read it before arguing with the checker.

frozen_note: Conditions KEYS are identity three times over: Player.conditions stores the
English name into the save, conditionSlug() turns it into the #anchor the
info sidebar opens, and player.js/conditions_section.jsx compare it against
hardcoded sets (HP_DERIVED, POSITIVE, ABILITY_PARAM). Italian condition
names live in src/data/it/names.json instead.
Enums/* are enum values used across the app. 'Shop Types'/#/Name is matched
by shop.js against the saved ShopType. Link is a slug.

glossary_exempt.feat: Domains/Strength's 'you can perform a feat of strength' is a deed, not a talento -- the granted power is a one-round Strength bonus and has nothing to do with feats.

frozen_note: School — regex-matched: augmentSummoning.js tests /\(summoning\)/i and
getSpellFocusBonus compares the school for Spell Focus and specialisation.
Level — 'Sor/Wiz 2' is parsed by player.js with a per-class key regex.
Components — 'V, S, M, F' already reads the same in Italian.
Name, Link, id — identity; Name is also a lookup key in augmentSummoning.
Category — proficiency.js does startsWith('simple'|'martial'|'exotic').
Name — shop.js and player.js match saved inventory rows by Name.
Link, Base, id — identity and cross-references.
Type/Subtype/Critical/Dmg (S)/Dmg (M)/Range — mechanical values shown as-is.
Italian item names go in src/data/it/names.json.
Name — featEffects.js and player.js match feats by lowercased name
(FINESSE_NAMED_WEAPONS, 'simple weapon proficiency', qualifying.add(...)).
Tags — filter values. suggestedClass — class enum keys.
Name — player.js looks skills up by name in five places and falls back to
the literal 'Knowledge'. Saved characters store skill names.
Characteristic — 'Int'/'Cha' ability keys.
Synergies from/to — skill names used as lookup keys.
weaponProficiency — proficiency.js matches 'Simple weapons' by prefix.
hitDice/baseAttack/fortSave/reflexSave/willSave/castingAbility — enum codes.
classSkills — a comma-joined list of skill names, matched against skills.json.
favoredEnemyTypes — matched against a creature's `type`.
The classes/* keys themselves are the class names the whole app runs on.
races/* keys and `size`, `favoredClass`, `skill`, `weaponProficiency`,
`weaponFamiliarity`, languages — all matched against other data or code.
traits/#/name is display-only but short and repeated; it goes to names.json
rather than being translated in place.
type/kind/mode/reset/result/save/casterClass/spell — enum codes and spell
slugs read by src/lib/trap. ref is identity. name goes to names.json.
attack / fullAttack — PARSED by attackParser.parseAttacks, which splits on
'and'/'or' and reads 'melee'/'ranged'. Animal companions, familiars, special
mounts and wild shape all recompute from these strings. Translating them
silently breaks every companion in the app.
size/type/subtypes — mechanical (size modifiers, filters, favored enemy).
raw — the display half of a parsed stat line; keep it in step with the
numbers beside it. skills/feats/specialQualities/specialAttacks are name
lists; they belong in names.json, not here.
environment/organization/treasure/alignment/advancement are prose but are
not yet on the list — decide them as one batch, with a grep, before adding.
Same as monsters.json — attack/fullAttack are parsed.
Same as monsters.json — attack/fullAttack are parsed.
The top-level keys are ability slugs; `name` goes to names.json.
The top-level keys are ability slugs; `name` goes to names.json.
name — deity names are proper nouns and stay as they are.
domains — matched against tables.json Domains. ethical/moral — alignment enums.
favoredWeapon — matched against items.json.
Nothing to translate: scrolls carry only Name and Link, and the Name is
built from the spell ('Scroll of Acid splash'). It is composed for display
in src/lib/item/scrolls.js — translate it there, not here.
Only link/type/role — all identity or enum codes.
GENERATED by scripts/build-rules.mjs from obsidian-vault/dnd-rules/.
Never edit either this file or src/data/it/rules.json by hand -- the
next write into the notes folder overwrites both. Translate the
markdown in obsidian-vault/dnd-rules-it/ and re-run the generator.
slug -- the topic id a link and the tab route resolve against.
anchor -- the section id, slugged from the ENGLISH heading, so it is
stable across languages and is what an in-note link points at.
level -- 2 or 3; the app renders the outline from it.
units_aware_numbers -- the ONLY file with it on. Everywhere else the
Italian keeps the English unit ("30 piedi") and convertUnitsInText
converts at render, so both sides say 30 and the plain number comparison
is correct and stricter. These notes are prose rather than data: the
English is mixed ("5-ft step", "9 m (6 sq)") and the Italian is metric
throughout, so the same rule is written with different numbers. Counting
a measurement by its metric magnitude compares the distance instead of
the digits -- and 30 ft rendered as 3 m still fails, because it is 9 m.

glossary_exempt.round: the English verb -- 'round the corner', 'round to the nearest multiple of 7' -- not the unit of time.
glossary_exempt.Str: the class abbreviation in classes.md's abbreviation table: 'Sorcerer (Str)' is Stregone, and the Italian says Str too.
glossary_exempt.weapon: 'breath weapon' is 'soffio' in Italian and never 'arma'.
glossary_exempt.character: 'a grossly out-of-character act' is 'fuori carattere', not 'personaggio'.
